cosy-lesson.title: Antidepressants Are So Not a Big Deal

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Antidepressant – A medication used to alleviate clinical depression or anxiety.

p.em: Example: The song celebrates taking antidepressants in a joyous, high-energy 1920s tap dance.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stigma – A mark of disgrace associated with a particular circumstance or treatment.

p.em: Example: Taking daily medication for mental health still carries an unfair social stigma.

cosy-blockquote.p: Chemical – Relating to chemistry, or a substance used in or produced by chemical processes.

p.em: Example: Depression is a chemical imbalance in the brain, not a personal flaw.

cosy-blockquote.p: Serotonin – A neurotransmitter that regulates mood, sleep, and emotional stability.

p.em: Example: If your brain doesn't produce enough serotonin, store-bought medication is fine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Normal – Conforming to a standard, usual, or typical type.

p.em: Example: Normalizing mental health treatment helps millions of people seek help.

cosy-blockquote.p: Therapy – Treatment intended to relieve or heal a disorder, especially mental.

p.em: Example: Combining therapy with prescribed medication yields the best long-term outcomes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Shame – A painful feeling of humiliation or distress caused by consciousness of guilt.

p.em: Example: There should be zero shame in taking medication to stay healthy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prescription – An instruction written by a medical practitioner authorizing a medicine.

p.em: Example: Getting a prescription for mental health is no different than getting glasses.

cosy-blockquote.p: Imbalance – A lack of proportion or relation between corresponding things.

p.em: Example: Addressing a brain imbalance with science is a sensible health decision.

cosy-blockquote.p: Routine – A sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

p.em: Example: Taking a pill each morning becomes a simple, unremarkable daily routine.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: He takes an antidepressant for be happy → Correct: He takes an antidepressant to be happy / to balance his mood ((Use 'to + infinitive' for purpose.))
Incorrect: There is no shame for taking medication → Correct: There is no shame in taking medication ((Use 'shame in + gerund'.))
Incorrect: It is a chemical imbalance of the brain → Correct: It is a chemical imbalance in the brain ((Use 'imbalance in' a organ/system.))
